subject: POC infra MAP & onboarding checklist — API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Amanda Torres <amanda@eoshealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Lang <chris.lang@eoshealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — infra details and ask

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. EOS Health would like to run a 4-week POC focused on inference latency for clinician-facing summaries. Before we lock dates, our infra team needs a clear mutual action plan that includes the following so we can approve network changes this week:

- How Redwood provisions API keys and org-level access (who is the admin)
- IP allowlist requirements and an initial CIDR set we can put on our firewall
- VPC peering: steps and whether we need dedicated subnets or specific routing rules
- Expected support window for the first week of traffic (we plan some stress tests)

I've attached a simplified network diagram (eos_network_diagram.pdf) and our internal timeline. Can you draft a MAP with explicit owner/responsibility lines and an estimated close date for the evaluation? Our target is to complete the POC and decide on Dedicated Reserved Capacity by 2026-11-24.

Appreciate it — I can loop in our DevOps alias (devops@eoshealth.com) if helpful.

Best,
Amanda
Amanda Torres
Head of Product, EOS Health
@eoshealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Chris Lang <chris.lang@eoshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — infra details and ask

Hi Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Draft MAP attached (redwood_map_draft_20261103.pdf) with owners, dates, and success criteria. High-level answers inline below and the MAP has a short checklist we can convert into tasks for your DevOps team.

1) API keys & org setup
- We can create a dedicated org for EOS with a single admin account and scoped service API keys for the POC.
- Admin API key issuance: security review + signed MSA (if required). We can issue dev/test keys immediately and rotate to prod keys on go/no-go.
- Action owner: Hannah (Redwood) to provision admin, Amanda/Chris to confirm admin identity.

2) IP allowlist
- Minimum requirement: allow the following egress CIDR for Redwood edge proxies: 34.82.16.0/24 and 34.82.17.0/24 (examples; final CIDRs confirmed by infra).
- We recommend adding a short-lived wildcard during stress tests and then tightening to the two CIDRs above.
- Action owner: EOS DevOps to apply; Soojin to verify connectivity.

3) VPC peering
- We support two options: managed VPC peering (Redwood peers to your VPC) or proxy-based secure integration (no peering).
- For peering: need a single /24 dedicated subnet for peering endpoints, appropriate route table entries, and cross-account IAM/peering consent.
- Action owner: Karthik (Redwood SE) will provide the exact terraform snippets and routing guidance.

4) Support window & stress tests
- Our on-call SE will be available during the first full-day stress test with dedicated channel in Slack.
- If you confirm target dates, we will reserve canary capacity for the initial tests.

I've included the proposed timeline in the MAP: baseline setup (week 1), integration & smoke tests (week 2), performance ramp (week 3), evaluation & decision (week 4). Proposed finish: 2026-11-24 to align with your decision milestone.

Please review the attached MAP and tell us where you'd like edits. If you prefer, we can convert the checklist into a HubSpot mutual action plan and share the link.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Torres <amanda@eoshealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Chris Lang <chris.lang@eoshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — infra details and ask

Amanda — quick technical notes to iron out before your infra team opens firewall changes. I'm adding the checklist items I need from you and a short sequence for peering.

Required from EOS for API key/org provisioning:
- Confirm which email(s) will be the org admins (we'll create the org slug).
- Decide whether service keys should be scoped to specific models or full access for POC.

IP allowlist specifics (recommended temporary values for testing):
- Redwood edge egress: 34.82.16.0/24, 34.82.17.0/24
- Control-plane access (for metrics/webhooks): 34.82.18.0/27 (limited)

VPC peering sequence (if you choose peering):
1) EOS creates a peering request from your VPC console referencing redwood-peer-acc (we'll provide the account id)
2) Redwood accepts and we exchange route table entries
3) Your infra adds a /24 route for the peering endpoint; avoid overlapping CIDRs
4) We validate via mutual NAT and sample traffic to a staging endpoint

Questions / caveats:
- If you prefer proxy integration, you avoid peering complexity but latency profile differs; we can provide a perf delta based on past POC data.
- For stress tests, please provide expected peak concurrent requests and average token lengths so we can allocate canary capacity.

HubSpot link to the draft MAP (converted to an action plan): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

I can drop the terraform snippet and route table example in a follow-up — let me know which option you prefer (peering vs proxy).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Next steps for us: DevOps will schedule a maintenance window on 2026-11-09 to apply initial firewall rules. We'll attach your vpc-peering request after we get the terraform snippet.

If everything else is aligned, our decision-makers are expecting a one-page summary of owners and the target close date (2026-11-24). Can you send that final one-pager and the peering checklist?

Thanks — looping in devops.

Best,
Amanda
